title: Hamas releases US-Israeli hostage Edan Alexander
body:
On Monday 12 May 2025, Hamas released Edan Alexander, a 21-year-old US-Israeli dual citizen, after more than 19 months in captivity, CBS News reported. He was believed to be the last living US citizen held hostage in Gaza. Alexander grew up in New Jersey, moved to Israel and was serving in the Israeli military when Hamas abducted him during the attack of 7 October 2023. Hamas had announced the decision on the evening of 11 May, saying it would free him without conditions following contacts with the US administration.

He was handed to the Red Cross and then to the Israel Defense Forces. The International Committee of the Red Cross confirmed a safe transfer of a hostage without naming him. US envoy Steve Witkoff travelled to the region before the release, and President Donald Trump left Washington that day for a trip to Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. Trump congratulated Alexander's family on Truth Social and called the release a good-faith step toward ending the war, crediting mediators Qatar and Egypt.

Israel's Prime Minister's Office said it had committed only to a safe corridor for the release, not to a ceasefire or to freeing prisoners. Hamas said it was ready to start intensive talks on a final agreement, a prisoner exchange and an independent body to administer Gaza. The Hostages and Missing Families Forum welcomed the news and called for a comprehensive deal to free the remaining captives. CBS also reported that Israel had reportedly blocked food and medical aid from entering Gaza for nearly three months, and that Hamas-run health authorities said Israeli strikes on a school-turned-shelter in Jabaliya killed 16 people.
